chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The part is one of ten, because the mountains are ten, and the birds are four'.
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'part' (juz') mean in Shia inheritance law according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the term 'part' (juz') in bequests refers specifically to one-tenth, grounding this legal definition in a numerical analogy involving ten mountains and four birds. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of linguistic precision in Islamic jurisprudence, where common terms are interpreted through established semantic conventions to determine fractional shares in inheritance law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The ‘part’ is one from ten, because the mountains were ten, and the birds were four’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Aban ibn Th’alabah who has narrated the following: “
Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘A part is one-tenth because the mountains were ten and the birds were four.’”
